the most suitable surface for exterior applications is the one obtained by planing at a low speed (0.2 m/s), whereas the best surface for interior applications is the one planed at high speed (0.4 m/s).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the moisture uptake, surface free energy and adhesion of wood surfaces is influenced by the cutting speed (in defibration), storage time (in defibration and milling), wood location (juvenile, mature and heartwood) (in milling) and surface roughness (in milling).
the surface properties of Douglas-fir wood are influenced by the cutting speed, the storage time, the position in the stem and the cutting process.
it is necessary to have a good knowledge of the wood surface characteristics to be able to produce surfaces with the best possible properties for the application in question.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wood is a complex material and that its properties are strongly influenced by the cutting process.
, for the Douglas-fir species, the most important parameter to consider is the duration of surface storage before finishing or bonding.
the storage of surfaces is the most critical parameter in the production of surfaces that can be coated or glued.
